nodes.name: Most teams need pages that are not the main app: a blog,…
nodes.text: Most teams need pages that are not the main app: a blog, help articles, release notes, a roadmap, a launch page. They end up in a separate tool with its own accounts, its own permissions and no connection to the context the team already maintains.

nodes.name: Grid is a page and layout editor that lives inside the…
nodes.text: Grid is a page and layout editor that lives inside the same workspace as everything else. People edit in the browser; agents edit through the same operations, with their own explicit consent. Grid is in early access, with its own roles and its own connection capability. The pages you are reading—the blog, support, release notes and roadmap—are Grid pages.

nodes.name: A Grid page is built on a responsive grid. Vertical…
nodes.text: A Grid page is built on a responsive grid. Vertical layouts set columns and an optional maximum number of rows; horizontal layouts set rows and an optional maximum number of columns. A page can have up to twelve breakpoints, each with its own complete layout and optional per-node frame overrides, so a page can be designed for a phone and a desktop separately.

nodes.name: Pages can also flow like an article: nodes stack in…
nodes.text: Pages can also flow like an article: nodes stack in document order with natural text heights. Templates hold reusable layout settings. Applying a template is explicit, and editing a template never silently changes the pages made from it.

nodes.name: Pages hold formatted text, images, video, audio, shapes,…
nodes.text: Pages hold formatted text, images, video, audio, shapes, icons and separators, plus supported YouTube and Vimeo embeds. Text supports fitted sizing, drop caps, line height and uploaded fonts. Each node has its own placement and appearance, with separate opacity for foreground, background and borders.

nodes.name: Grid has its own asset library at each location. Media and…
nodes.text: Grid has its own asset library at each location. Media and fonts in a page always come from Grid assets, never from private Memory assets, so publishing a page can never expose a file from another library.

nodes.name: Grid was designed for agents from the start. External…
nodes.text: Grid was designed for agents from the start. External agents use `grid_*` tools through the NullDull MCP server and CLI; inside the console, Null offers Read and Work modes. Work mode needs current editor or manager access and a complete read of a page before changing it. Every save names the version it replaces and keeps a receipt, so a retried save doesn’t apply twice.

nodes.name: Agents can also turn Markdown into a page through the Grid…
nodes.text: Agents can also turn Markdown into a page through the Grid API. Headings, lists, quotes, code and tables keep their structure. HTML and images are rejected rather than silently dropped; media is added explicitly from uploaded Grid assets.

nodes.name: Saving a page keeps it private. Publishing is an explicit…
nodes.text: Saving a page keeps it private. Publishing is an explicit browser action for Grid managers: choose a content pool, a slug, a summary and an optional cover image, and publish that exact saved version. An agent’s edit permission never includes publishing.

nodes.name: Withdrawing is just as explicit: unpublishing a page or…
nodes.text: Withdrawing is just as explicit: unpublishing a page or disabling its pool removes its public URLs immediately. Published pages are delivered through a public read API that takes a workspace API key. The React renderer and the Grid core library are open packages on npm, and the same renderer draws the editor’s preview and the public pages you are reading now.
